events.credibility_reason: Eight versions in about four months with a title change (scope may have shifted), no expert engagement found, and if finite complexity were automatic it would be an unremarked resolution of a landmark problem; the full text and the definition of finite complexity were never read. Established authors with a serious method and no identified error, so doubtful rather than set aside.
Unreviewed, attribution disputed, described only through secondary sources; in any case a different problem (soficity).

why: The statement asks for homotopy invariance of higher signatures for all groups. If the (rational) strong Novikov conjecture holds for a class of groups, the Novikov conjecture holds for that class. So the class-of-groups results (Gong–Wu–Yu, Gong–Wu–Xie–Yu, Oyono-Oyono–Yu, Zhang, Tian–Yu) are cases. Tian–Yu is the close call. The record cannot show that finite-complexity embeddings exist for every countable group, and Wikipedia and the absence of any reaction both point to a proper class, so I scored it as a case rather than whole. The relative, equivariant coarse, Banach and codimension-2 transfer results answer changed questions, so they are variants. Wang assumes the conjecture, so it is none. The Astra and Fournier-Facio non-sofic results concern a different problem, so they are variants. On AI: Astra's AI role belongs to soficity, not Novikov, and its systems[] is empty here. No Novikov event credits any AI system (F13). Gong–Wu–Xie–Yu (first posted October 2023) stays pre-snapshot because its revisions show no new mathematics.
doubts: Tian–Yu's full text was unreadable. If finite complexity holds for all countable groups, that event would be whole (claimed), and its acknowledgements were never checked for AI. Novikov for groups of finite decomposition complexity was probably known before Oyono-Oyono–Yu (their abstract calls theirs a 'geometric proof'), so it may be a new proof of a known case. The record does not establish this, so I scored it as a case. The GAFA and Advances journal acceptances rest on unopened search snippets.
